newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela's electricity rate rise not approved yet.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela's electricity rate rise not approved yet.

text.p: The Venezuelan government has taken no decision yet on widely expected electricity tariff increases, a top government official said on Tuesday.
"There is no decision yet on electricity rate rises," deputy Energy and Mines Minister Evanan Romero told reporters.
"The amount of the (rate) adjustment and its timing have not been decided," he said, in response to almost daily media reports that the increases are about to be announced.
El Universal newspaper said earlier this month the electricity rates would rise by an average 25 per cent in May, and then in 1.25 percent increments until the hike reached 30 percent in total.

The government on April 18 approved a framework to govern electricity tariff rises but government officials were quick to stress that the increases would go into effect only after President Rafael Caldera gives the final approval.
Stock market bellwether Electricidad de Caracas has long pressed for tariff increases, with market analysts expecting between a 15 and 20 percent rise for the company.
